english.note: Use this for “total” meaning absolute or utter, as in a total failure.
Use this for the sense of sheer or utter, as in “pure madness” or “a pure fool.”
Use this for something that is complete, utter, or pure in the relevant quality.
Use this before a noun or adjective when complete is an emphatic intensifier, as in “a complete bastard.”
Use this before a description when proper means complete, utter, or downright, as in an utter fool.
Use this for the colloquial emphatic sense of “utter” or “absolute,” especially before a noun such as 十足嘅傻仔.
